chapters.title: Philosophical Roots & Pre-Scientific Thought
chapters.description: Examine how ancient philosophy, mind-body dualism, British empiricism, and 19th-century physiology paved the way for a scientific study of mind.

chapters.title: The Birth of Experimental Psychology & Structuralism
chapters.description: Witness the birth of psychology as an independent laboratory science with Wilhelm Wundt in 1879, psychophysics, and Titchener's Structuralism.

chapters.title: Functionalism, Evolutionary Thought & Pragmatism
chapters.description: Discover how Darwinian evolution inspired William James and American functionalists to study the adaptive purpose of human consciousness.

chapters.title: The Psychoanalytic Revolution & Psychodynamics
chapters.description: Explore Sigmund Freud's discovery of the unconscious mind, psychosexual stages, defense mechanisms, and Neo-Freudian expansions by Jung and Adler.

chapters.title: The Rise of Behaviorism
chapters.description: Trace psychology's radical turn toward observable behavior through Pavlov's conditioning, Watson's manifesto, and Skinner's operant technology.

chapters.title: Gestalt Psychology & The Humanistic Movement
chapters.description: Investigate the Gestalt revolt against elementalism and the emergence of Humanistic 'Third Force' psychology led by Rogers and Maslow.

chapters.title: The Cognitive Revolution & Neuropsychology
chapters.description: Analyze the shift away from behaviorism toward internal mental processes, the computer metaphor of mind, and modern cognitive neuroscience.

chapters.title: Contemporary Trends, Diversity & the Replication Crisis
chapters.description: Unpack the challenges of cross-cultural psychology, gender and diversity in historical research, and the modern Open Science revolution.
